subject: Parser Warning from Double For Loop

messages.author: 7c8f82135c6ac2b7
messages.subject: Parser Warning from Double For Loop
parts:
Hello,

I am getting a parser warning when running a double for loop in a "transformed parameters" block. Here is my model (a hierarchical MA(1) time series model with different lengths of observations sequences for each agent):

data {
                int<lower=0> I;
int<lower=0> M;
int<lower=1> periods[I];
matrix[I,M] y;
}
parameters {
real alpha[I];
real beta[I];
real<lower=0> sigma[I];
real mu1;
real mu2;
real<lower=0> sigma_mu1;
real<lower=0> sigma_mu2;
}
transformed parameters {
        matrix[I,M] epsilon;
for (j in 1:I) {
epsilon[j,1] = y[j,1] - alpha[j];
for (t in 2:periods[j]) {
epsilon[j,t] = (y[j,t] - alpha[j] - beta[j] * epsilon[j,t-1]);
}
}
}
model {
mu1 ~ normal(0,2);
mu2 ~ normal(0,2);
sigma_mu1 ~ gamma(2,0.01);
sigma_mu2 ~ gamma(2,0.01);
for (i in 1:I) {
alpha[i] ~ normal(mu1,sigma_mu1);
beta[i] ~ normal(mu2,sigma_mu2);
sigma[i] ~ gamma(1,2);
for (t in 2:periods[i]) {
y[i,t] ~ normal(alpha[i] + beta[i] * epsilon[i,t-1],sigma[i]);
}
}
}

 
The error I get is 

ERROR at line 20

 17: matrix[I,M] epsilon
 18: for (j in 1:I) {
 19: epsilon[j,1] = y[j,1] - alpha[j];
  ^
 20: for (t in 2:periods[j]) {

PARSER EXPECTED: "}"
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name=model_name
, :
   failed to parse Stan model 'weekly_ma1' due to the above error.
Calls: stan -> stan_model -> stanc
Execution halted

I am running R version 3.3.2 and Rstan version 2.9.0-3 on a Linux server. I understand this is not the latest version of Rstan, but I have no administrative access on this server and the administrators are often difficult to deal with w.r.t. updating software packages. Essentially, I am looking for a work-around with the current version if possible.

Thanks,

- Nick Pretnar

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Parser Warning from Double For Loop
parts:
This might be as simple as switching from "=" to "<-" for assignment. I don't think we introduced "=" for assignment until version 2.10, so if you're running 2.9.x then the problem might just be that 

 epsilon[j,t] = ...

should be 

 epsilon[j,t] <- ...

I haven't checked if there are other problems with the code but that would be the first thing to try I think.

Jonah
